'''Anicet Francois Dybantsa Jr.''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|ɑː|n|i|ˈ|s|eɪ}} {{respell|ah|nee|SAY}}, {{IPAc-en|d|iː|ˈ|b|ɑː|n|t|s|ɑː}} {{respell|dee|BAHNT|sah}}; born January 29, 2007) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Dybantsa played one year of [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]], earning the [[Julius Erving Award]] after [[List of NCAA Division I men's basketball season scoring leaders|leading the nation in scoring]] for the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2025–26 season]], prior to being selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the Wizards in the [[2026 NBA draft]]. He is also a member of the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|U.S. national under-19 team]], earning a gold medal at the [[2025 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] and [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|tournament MVP]] honors.

== Early life ==
Anicet Francois Dybantsa Jr. was born on January 29, 2007, in [[Boston]], Massachusetts, and grew up in [[Brockton, Massachusetts|Brockton]] where he attended [[Saint Sebastian's School]].<ref name="CBS Boston">{{cite web |last1=Geagan |first1=Matt |last2=Roche |first2=Dan |title=Top basketball recruit and Brockton native AJ Dybantsa playing in Boston Wednesday night |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/aj-dybantsa-utah-prep-homecoming-top-recruit-boston-brockton-ncaa-nba-basketball/ |website=CBS Boston |access-date=November 3, 2025 |date=November 6, 2024 |quote=Born in Boston and raised in Brockton, the presumptive No. 1 pick in the 2026 NBA Draft will enjoy a homecoming on Wednesday night. |archive-date=November 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251106042833/https://www.cbsnews.com/boston/news/aj-dybantsa-utah-prep-homecoming-top-recruit-boston-brockton-ncaa-nba-basketball/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="The Boston Globe">{{cite web |last=Gasper |first=Christopher L. |title=The best Mass. basketball prospect in decades returns home — and it might be your only shot to see him before he makes it big |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/10/31/sports/nba-aj-dybantsa-grind-session-emmanuel-boston/ |website=The Boston Globe |access-date=January 21, 2026 |date=October 31, 2024 |quote=Boston-born and Brockton-raised AJ Dybantsa. |archive-date=November 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241106224541/https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/10/31/sports/nba-aj-dybantsa-grind-session-emmanuel-boston/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His father Ace was born in the [[Republic of the Congo]] and later moved to [[Grigny, Essonne|Grigny]], France, while his mother Chelsea is from [[Jamaica]].

He was named the 2023 Massachusetts Boys' Basketball Gatorade Player of the Year following his freshman season after averaging 19.1 points, 9.6 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.5 blocks per game.<ref name="ProlificPrepTransfer">{{Cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=June 15, 2023 |title=High school basketball: Top-ranked Class of 2026 prospect A.J. Dybantsa transfers to Prolific Prep. |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/m/news/S1zeK71poE-UpMRiUmVv7g/high-school-basketball-top-ranked-class-of-2026-prospect-aj-dybantsa-transfers-to-prolific-prep.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618021158/https://www.maxpreps.com/m/news/S1zeK71poE-UpMRiUmVv7g/high-school-basketball-top-ranked-class-of-2026-prospect-aj-dybantsa-transfers-to-prolific-prep.htm |archive-date=June 18, 2023 |access-date=July 11, 2023 |website=[[MaxPreps]]}}</ref> Dybantsa helped lead Saint Sebastian's to the [[NEPSAC]] Class A state championship, but lost to [[Milton Academy]] 77–76.<ref name="2023U16USA">{{Cite news |last=Gasper |first=Christopher L. |date=June 8, 2023 |title=He's 16, the top prospect in his class, and playing for Team USA. How does AJ Dybantsa stay focused amid the hype? |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/06/08/sports/aj-dybantsa-basketball-prospect/ |url-status=live |url-access=limited |access-date=July 11, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230711203111/https://www.bostonglobe.com/2023/06/08/sports/aj-dybantsa-basketball-prospect/ |archive-date=July 11, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
On December 10, 2024, Dybantsa announced on ''[[First Take (talk show)|First Take]]'' that he would be committing to [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] as he wanted to play basketball without off-court distractions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 19, 2025 |title=AJ Dybantsa shares why he choose BYU and why he loves being in Utah |url=https://www.basketballnetwork.net/college/aj-dybantsa-shares-why-he-choose-byu-and-why-he-loves-being-in-utah |website=Basketball Network |access-date=November 4, 2025 |archive-date=June 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260624101004/https://www.basketballnetwork.net/college/aj-dybantsa-shares-why-he-choose-byu-and-why-he-loves-being-in-utah |url-status=live }}</ref> He became the highest-ranked committed recruit to join BYU in program history.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2024 |title=Dybantsa, projected top NBA pick, chooses BYU |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/42892244 |access-date=December 10, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |archive-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723193928/https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/42892244 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On January 24, 2026, Dybantsa passed [[Danny Ainge]] for the most points posted by a BYU freshman in a game, recording 43 points during a 91–78 victory over [[2025–26 Utah Utes men's basketball team|Utah]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dybantsa sets BYU freshman scoring record as Cougars cruise|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/47719618|access-date=April 30, 2026|website=ESPN.com|language=en|date=January 24, 2026|others=Contributed by The Associated Press|archive-date=July 23, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260723193921/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/47719618|url-status=live}}</ref> On April 22, Dybantsa declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]], in which he was projected as a potential first overall pick.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48571489 |title=Potential No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa declares for NBA draft |first=Myron |last=Medcalf |website=ESPN.com |date=April 23, 2026 |access-date=April 23, 2026 |archive-date=April 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260424090017/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48571489 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 23, 2026, Dybantsa was selected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Youngmisuk |first=Ohm |title=Wizards opt for BYU's AJ Dybantsa with top pick of NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49158973 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=June 23, 2026 |date=June 23, 2026 |archive-date=June 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260624002633/https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49158973 |url-status=live }}</ref> He signed a four-year rookie contract worth $66.91 million on July 2, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |last=Finberg |first=Greg |title=AJ Dybantsa signs rookie contract worth $66.9 million |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/aj-dybantsa-signs-rookie-contract-210404544.html |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=5 July 2026 |date=2 July 2026 |archive-date=July 5, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260705192307/https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/aj-dybantsa-signs-rookie-contract-210404544.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
